chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about the sale of fresh juice from those who make it into wine, so he said: 'Selling it from those who cook it or make it into vinegar is more beloved to me, and I see no harm in the first [selling it to those who make it into wine].'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell fresh grape juice to wine-makers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the permissibility (jawaz) of selling fresh grape juice to wine-makers and the preferability (istihbab) of selling it to vinegar-makers, reflecting the Shia principle of avoiding direct causes of intoxication (sabab al-khamr) while maintaining commercial flexibility. This ruling highlights the nuanced approach in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* where a transaction is valid even if the buyer uses it for an impermissible purpose, provided the seller does not explicitly intend the sale for that specific use.
